> location set gets walked on every minting rather than the nearest one.]**

**The occurrence it is derived from, in one paragraph, because the shape
matters more than the instance.** Pass 23.3's dependency was amended from
23.2 to 26.0 on 2026-08-05 in exactly **one** place — decision 025's
registration note. `docs/decisions/023-…md` §7.4 still said *"Depends on
23.2"* and **correctly so**, being append-only. But `ROADMAP.md`'s own
Backlog entry for 23.3 carried the same stale sentence, **copied from 023
§7.4 and editable all along**. A day later a filing read that Backlog
entry — **the single most obvious place to look** — and reported a
dependency-graph defect that did not exist. **The victim was the careful
reader, not the careless one**, which is why the duty is worth stating.

**Why the append-only convention GUARANTEES this rather than merely
permitting it.** Every amendment to a decided fact necessarily leaves an
older, still-authoritative-looking statement behind in
`docs/decisions/`. The project's answer up to now — *"the amendment is
filed elsewhere"* — **is the fork**. The editable mirror must therefore
do two jobs, not one: carry the new fact, **and** say it outranks the
record it was copied from.

**The mechanical form of the duty, so it is cheap enough to actually
perform:** at amendment time, grep the fact's **distinctive phrase**
(*"Depends on 23.2"*), and fix or annotate every hit. Under a minute, in
the filing that is already open. **Nothing detects a skipped
propagation** — `tools/check-ledger-numbers.py` counts IDs, not agreement
between statements of the same fact — so the duty is the only guard there
is.

**Its sibling, already in force and never treated as optional:** the
`FEATURES.md` maintenance contract (*"update `FEATURES.md` in the SAME
filing as every `ROADMAP.md` update"*). That contract is this duty
restricted to capability rows; this is the same obligation generalised to
any fact stated in more than one place. **Read them as one discipline.**

**Related:** **R87**'s 2026-08-07 broadening — the *reporting* half of the
same failure. This duty stops the stale statement existing; R87's
document-kind check stops a reader believing it once it does.

#### ★ SECOND INSTANCE (2026-08-07, found by the Pass 20.2/20.3 fork) — a RAG **GAP marker** that outlived the decision closing it. Different pair of documents, same failure

The founding instance was a **fact** copied from an append-only decision
record into `ROADMAP.md` and left stale (*"Depends on 23.2"*). This one is
an **obligation**, and it ran the other way:

- **The producing side** —
  `D:\Dev\Rag-Specialized\Acrobat_Features\forms__field_creation_minimums.md`
  wrote, of a zero-option choice field: *"**GAP, flagged explicitly**:
  this is a real edge case … pdfce must decide deliberately rather than
  infer."*
- **The consuming side** — decision 020 §6 F3 **decided it on 2026-08-03**:
  *"Empty `/Opt` is ALLOWED and disclosed"*, with the exact warning text.
- **Nothing propagated back.** Four days later the fork building choice
  fields read the RAG, took the GAP at face value, and **decided to
  REFUSE** — the opposite of the ruling. It caught its own error only by
  re-reading decision 020 for an unrelated reason, and reversed.

**Why this earns a note here rather than a shrug.** The duty as written
covers *facts* stated in two documents. **An obligation marker is not a
fact — it is a claim that a decision is still OPEN**, and it is the one
kind of statement whose staleness actively recruits work. A stale fact
misleads a reader; **a stale GAP marker commissions a redecision, and the
redecision can come out the other way**, which is exactly what happened.

**So the duty extends, in substance and without a new number:** *when a
decision record CLOSES a question that some other document flagged as
open, the closure is filed against the flagging document in the same
filing — or, where that document belongs to another agent, the dispatch
to annotate it is named in the filing.* **Annotating a discharged GAP is
part of discharging it.**

**Same asymmetry as the founding instance, and worth naming again: the
victim is the CAREFUL reader.** Only an agent who actually consults the
Acrobat RAG before deciding can be misled by a stale GAP in it. The one
who decides from memory sails past.

**Its sibling one level up:** the 2026-08-06 `FEATURES.md` Acrobat-column
finding — *an obligation recorded only on the producing side is not
recorded at all*. **Read together, the pair says an obligation needs a
record on BOTH sides: one that says it is owed, and one that says it was
paid.** This instance had the first and never got the second.

**Not fixed by the filing that found it** — `Acrobat_Features` is
`pdfcer-acrobat-librarian`'s exclusive territory, the same way
`PDF_Spec` is `pdfcer-spec-librarian`'s. **Dispatch recommended:** annotate
that GAP as closed by decision 020 §6 F3 and sweep the file's remaining
GAP markers for the same condition. **Nothing else in the project will
notice.**

### Filing-heading ordinal spelling — RULED 2026-08-26 (269th filing): numerals are acceptable going forward; the 268th's heading is not renormalized

Every `SESSION_LOG.md` filing heading before the 268th spelled its
ordinal out (`two-hundred-and-sixty-seventh filing`). The 268th wrote
`(268th filing)` instead, and `tools/check-ledger-numbers.py`'s
`FILING_HEADING` regex — written to expect only the alphabetic spelling
— never matched it: the heading was never handed to `ordinal_to_int()`,
never landed in the `unparsed` list, and the gate's own `UNCHECKED`
failure report — which exists precisely to make an unrecognised heading
loud — had nothing to report. The gate printed `SESSION_LOG filings :
267 -> next free is 268` with 268 already on disk, and still summarised
`ledger-numbers: clean`. **Fixed by the engineer this same filing**: the
regex now recognises `(<anything> filing)` and decides nothing;
`ordinal_to_int()` decides and returns `None` — reported as `UNCHECKED`
and failed — for anything it cannot parse. Numeral ordinals now parse
correctly, and the re-run reads `SESSION_LOG filings : 268 -> next free
is 269`. Filed as an instance of the established under-reporting-gate
class (first named at the 183rd filing: *"a gate that under-reports is
byte-indistinguishable from a green one"*) rather than a new one; no new
standing rule minted, per that class's existing coverage.

**Ruling: numerals are acceptable, and are the preferred spelling going
forward.** Two reasons, both drawn from this project's own history
rather than taste. First, a spelled-out ordinal is the harder format for
a machine to parse correctly — `ordinal_to_int()`'s own vocabulary has
had to be extended more than once as filings crossed spellings it did
not yet know (`hundredth`, `hundred-and-Nth`, documented at the 103rd
filing), each extension a place the parser could fail open instead of
closed; a numeral has no such vocabulary to be missing. Second, at the
filing counts this project has already reached, a spelled-out ordinal is
materially harder for a human to typo-check on sight than the number it
names.

**The 268th's heading is left as written.** Rewriting it to match a
convention decided after the fact would be editing an already-filed
`SESSION_LOG.md` entry — the same append-only discipline this document
applies to `Shipped` entries applies to itself. Both spellings are now
attested in the ledger from here forward; the checker accepts either,
and this ruling does not ask for a sweep of the 267 filings that came
before it.

### How a figure is filed (added 2026-08-07, twenty-third filing — ADOPTED AS STANDING PRACTICE, DELIBERATELY NOT A NUMBERED RULE)

**Two conventions, both nearly free, both about the SHAPE a number is
written in rather than about checking anything after the fact. `R167` is
NOT minted; the ceiling stays `R166`.**
**★ RE-AFFIRMED 2026-08-07 (twenty-ninth filing), ON THE ENGINEER'S EXPLICIT
RULING: `R167` STAYS FREE.** The byte-identity candidate the twenty-eighth
filing wrote up is **a RAG finding, not a rule.** Its four grounds hold, and
**the third is the one that decides it: *"validate every baseline" commissions
WORK, not CARE*** — the exact ground the **ablation candidate** was refused on
**the same day**. **Refusing it there and minting it here would make the bar
decorative**, and a bar that bends to whoever happens to be filing enforces
nothing. **This is now the second consecutive filing to leave `R167`
free, and both left it free for the same stated reason** — which is what a
bar looks like when it is real. **Ceiling `R166`; `R167` next free.**
They live here, beside the
same-filing propagation duty, for the same reason that duty does: **this is
a rule about how to file, so it belongs where an agent performing a filing
will meet it.** The binding statement for the agent that performs filings is
`.claude/agents/pdfcer-librarian.md` **hard rule 10**; this is its
project-visible half, so a reader auditing a filing can see what the filing
was supposed to do.

**1. FILE A TOTAL BESIDE ITS PER-ITEM FORM.**

> Write ***"5.24 s over 24,128 clips = 217 µs each"***, not ***"5.24 s"***.

**Why this is the whole mechanism, and not merely tidy.** A total and a
per-item mean are **the same fact in two forms**. Filing only one of them is
what makes a contradiction between two filings **unreachable** — not merely
unnoticed. Writing both **converts a SET-property (two filed numbers
disagree) into a SINGLE-CLAIM property (this line is wrong)**, and ordinary
one-claim review — the only kind of review anyone actually performs — can
catch the second and can never catch the first.

**The instance it was derived from.** `mask.fill_path` was filed at
**5.24 s over 24,128 clips** in one RAG file and at **8.3 µs page-sized** in
another. **5.24 s ÷ 24,128 = 217 µs. A 26× contradiction**, carried openly
for **two filings**, with the two figures **217 lines apart in the same
`index.md`**. Both were measured correctly; both were reviewed; neither was
wrong *on its own terms*. **The correction required no new measurement, only
division** — and the wrong figure had by then been the ranking key for a
work order for six hours and had **dispatched a fork on a false premise**.
**Had this convention existed, the contradiction would have been on the line
where it was written.**

**Corollary, because the division needs it: RECORD THE DENOMINATOR.** Had
`24,128` not been filed, the contradiction would have been **genuinely**
unreachable rather than merely unreached.

**2. PUT THE QUALIFIER IN THE TABLE LABEL, BECAUSE THE LABEL IS WHAT GETS
QUOTED.**

**The instance.** An ablation row's own label read ***"clip intersection
skipped entirely"*** — which is exactly right, and by construction means
*floor **plus** painting*. **Three lines below it**, prose read *"Painting
all 129,515 paths costs 0.87 seconds."* Painting alone is **~0.27 s**; the
floor is ~0.54 s. **The correct reading was printed above the incorrect one
for four filings, and the prose is the half that travelled** — into
`FEATURES.md`, into two decision entries, and into the sizing of every
painting-side optimisation.

**When a table row's label and the sentence under it can be read
independently, they will be.** So the qualifier goes in the **label**.

#### ★ NO CHECKER WAS BUILT, AND THE REASONS ARE RECORDED SO NOBODY RE-OPENS IT

A gate that extracts filed quantities and evaluates derived identities is
**conceivable, not cheap, and was judged NOT warranted** (R163's
carrier question, asked and answered):

1. **Extraction IS the job.** The figures live in English prose, markdown
   tables, amendment footers and commit messages, in units that vary (`s`,
   `µs`, `%`, `×`).
2. **Cross-configuration comparison MANUFACTURES contradictions rather than
   finding them.** 1× vs 2×; before vs after a fix; `--repeat 1` vs
   `--repeat 3`. Comparing two figures from different configurations
   produces false positives by construction, and **a gate that cries wolf
   enforces nothing** (`D:\dev\rag\rust\ci_gate_red_at_baseline_enforces_nothing.md`).
3. **The identity set is not enumerable in advance.** `total ÷ count` was
   obvious *after* the fact. Label-vs-prose is not an arithmetic identity at
   all, and the third instance in the same family (a doc comment refuted by
   `cfg!`) is a program-analysis question. **A carrier that catches only the
   first is not a carrier for this finding.**
4. **It commissions WORK, not CARE** — the same ground on which this project
   declined three standing-rule candidates in one week. A rule cannot
   schedule the building of a checker, and until the checker exists the rule
   is a reminder.

**These two conventions ARE the carrier — not a checker that computes
consistency, but a filing shape that makes a contradiction land inside a
single expression.** Cost: one division at write time.

**Full derivation, with all four instances:**
`D:\dev\rag\rust\a_record_can_carry_its_own_refutation_because_review_checks_claims_against_the_world.md`.
**Sibling in this section:** the same-filing propagation duty above — that
one stops a fact being stated inconsistently **across documents**; this one
stops a figure being stated in a form that **cannot** be checked at all.

### How you know a document is converging (added 2026-08-23, two-hundred-and-thirty-sixth filing — ADOPTED AS STANDING PRACTICE, DELIBERATELY NOT A NUMBERED RULE; `R216` STAYS FREE)

**The practice, in one line: after each round of repair on a document, name the
CLASS of what is left, not the count.** The class is the signal; the count is
noise.

**The founding observation, from five consecutive filings against one file
(`tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md`, `bd9844d` → `39b449f`):**

| round | what was found | class |
|---|---|---|
| 1–2 | `11 of 11` as an acceptance criterion, then as a measured result; `93 s` quoted as a baseline; `71.5×` derived from it | **wrong VALUES** |
| 3 | two pre/post boundary sentences pointing at different lines, neither at the boundary | **wrong REFERENCES** |
| 4 | a scope sentence false of its own section's tables; *"the table above"* crossing a section boundary | **wrong QUANTIFIER + wrong REFERENCE** |
| 5 | §10's twin scope sentence; *"the sentence above it"*; a universal beside an existential over a set of one; a referent named after a deleted label | **wrong QUANTIFIERS + wrong REFERENCES — and NO wrong values** |

⇒ **The number-shaped defects are swept out and the residue is the class only
READING catches.** That is a **stopping signal for one KIND of review** — grep,
gates, arithmetic cross-checks and hard rule 10's beside-its-operands convention
have all found everything they can find in this file — and simultaneously a
signal that **the remaining work cannot be delegated to any of them.**

**Why this is practice and not a rule.** It **prescribes no action**, so there is
nothing to oblige and nothing to check. Its value is that it is **free**: the
classes are already written down in the filings, and reading them off costs one
sentence. A rule saying *"classify your residue"* would commission **work, not
care** — the ground this project has now declined four standing-rule candidates
on.

**★★ The counter-caution, filed WITH it, because a stopping signal is exactly the
kind of finding that gets over-trusted.** *"No wrong values left"* is a statement
about the defects that have been **found**, not about the ones **present**. And
the residue is partly self-sustaining: **the 236th filing's Survivor C is a
quantifier defect introduced BY the repair of a quantifier defect** — the
replacement sentence carried a universal and an existential hedge over the same
one-member set. ⇒ **each round's repair re-seeds the residue class**, so class
stability is evidence about the *review instruments*, **not** evidence that the
document is finished. Reading it as the second is how a document stops being
read.

**Full derivation:**
`D:/dev/rag/rust/the_defect_class_left_after_repeated_repair_rounds_is_the_stopping_signal.md`.
**Sibling in this section:** *"How a figure is filed"* — that one makes a
contradiction land inside a single expression so ordinary review can catch it;
this one tells you when ordinary review has caught everything it is capable of.

#### ★★★★★ AMENDED 2026-08-23 (two-hundred-and-thirty-seventh filing, `a68498b`) — ROUND 6 FALSIFIES TWO OF THE THREE COMPONENTS ABOVE, AND PROMOTES THE COUNTER-CAUTION TO THE MAIN FINDING

**The text above is left standing**, per the append-only convention and per
`R215` (d): it is the record of what the practice claimed when it was adopted,
**and it was adopted one filing before the round that refuted it**, which is
itself the point.

| the practice's claim, above | round 6 (`a68498b`) |
|---|---|
| *"The number-shaped defects are swept out"* — **no wrong values left** | **FALSE.** Round 6 produced a **wrong count** (§9's *"three post-fix columns"*; the table has **four** columns, **two** post-fix, and the third item enumerated is a **note**, not a column) and a **wrong fraction** (this role's own *"two-thirds"*, where the answer is **one-half**) |
| the residue is *"wrong QUANTIFIERS + wrong REFERENCES"*, a stable class | **Half true, and it is not a RESIDUE — it is PRODUCTION.** Round 6 emitted a **fresh** wrong reference (*"the gap between `after` and `correct` is the whole subject of §9's last paragraph"* — the gap does not exist, `after` and `correct` are identical in **5 of 5** rows, and §9's last paragraph is a different one), of the class **round 5 declared structurally fixed** by promoting the boundary to a heading |
| ★★ counter-caution: *"each round's repair re-seeds the residue class"* | **CONFIRMED, AND MEASURED AT `n=3` CONSECUTIVE ROUNDS** — `641deb9` over-scoped, `39b449f` paired a universal with an existential hedge, `a68498b` miscounted the set. Same file, same sentence lineage, three generations |

**★★★★★ THE AMENDED FINDING, WHICH REPLACES THE HEADLINE ABOVE RATHER THAN
QUALIFYING IT: a stable defect class after repeated rounds is evidence that the
REPAIR PROCESS IS GENERATING ITS OWN INPUT, not evidence that the document is
approaching a fixed point.** The counter-caution was filed as a caveat; at `n=3`
it is **the dominant mechanism**, and the original headline reads as its
optimistic special case.

**★★★★ The class LADDER is retired.** The sequence was summarised as *wrong
**values** → wrong **pointers** → wrong **quantifiers** → wrong **antecedents***,
each round finding fewer and sharper defects. **That is a true description of
what each round FOUND FIRST. It is not a description of what the document
CONTAINS**, and the two were being conflated. Round 6 produced a wrong **count**
and a wrong **positional pointer** *simultaneously* — classes one and two, both
recorded as swept. ⇒ **the classes RECUR; they do not RETIRE**, and a reader who
takes the ladder literally stops looking one rung down, which is the failure
mode a stopping signal is most likely to cause.

**★★★ And the reviewer is inside the process, not outside it.** The 237th
filing's sweep of **its own** documents (the dispatch's item 7) found **four**
instances of the same shapes it had spent the day filing about: an ordinal
pointer naming the wrong column in the 234th filing's correction table, the
*"two-thirds"* fraction in **all three** of this role's documents, and
*"Everything below this line is unchanged from the previous handoff"* in
`NEXT_SESSION.md` — **false in the commit that wrote it**, and `R214` clause
(d)'s exact construction, **written by the filing that minted clause (d)** — and
★★★★★ **`"the third post-fix column"` in this practice's OWN RAG finding, which
is the copy that PROPAGATED into the next repair.**
⇒ **nothing in an append-only record reviews the reviewer**, so *"the residue
is the class only reading catches"* is incomplete: **it is the class only
reading catches, in a document nobody is reading with the same intent.**

**Still true, and not weakened:** grep, gates and arithmetic cross-checks
**have** found everything they can find in this file, and the remaining work
still cannot be delegated to any of them. **Still practice, not a rule** — it
prescribes no action, and the mint was **declined again** at `n=3` on coverage
rather than on instance count: `R214` clauses (c) and (d) already bind on a
repair's own sentence, so what round 6 shows is **non-application, not a gap**.
**`R216` stays free.**

#### ★★★★★ AMENDED AGAIN 2026-08-23 (two-hundred-and-thirty-eighth filing, `bc6c818`) — THE GENERATOR IS NAMED, AND THAT IS WHAT ENDED THE SEQUENCE

**Both texts above are left standing** — the original practice and its first
amendment — per the append-only convention and `R215` (d). They are the record of
what this practice claimed at rounds 5 and 6, and **this amendment explains them
rather than merely falsifying them**, which is the first time in the sequence
that has been possible.

**The round-7 disposition was DELETION, not repair.** `bc6c818` removed four
paragraphs from `tools/gen-scale-demo/README.md` §9 and wrote one short note in
their place. **All four owed repairs discharged**, three of them by that
deletion. It is the first round in seven whose owed-work list came out empty.

**★★★★★ THE FINDING, and it subsumes both texts above: a document that
annotates its own corrections has made its correction history part of its
CONTENT — and that part has no tests, no measurements and no reader who would
notice. It generates defects at a steady rate, and each repair adds another
sentence to the generator.**

**Measured across the six rounds**, which is why this is stronger than either
earlier reading:

| what | measured |
|---|---|
| defects in the **engineering content** (the arithmetic, the three `f32` limits, the drift formula, the table's values) | **0 after round 1.** Unchanged since `4af0c08` |
| defects in **sentences about a previous correction** | **all of them**, every round |
| rounds whose repair emitted a fresh defect of the class it repaired | **`n=4`** — `641deb9`, `39b449f`, `a68498b`, and **this role's own correction footers**, found by the 238th filing's item-8 sweep at **five sites across two documents** |

⇒ **THE CLASS WAS STABLE BECAUSE THE GENERATOR WAS STABLE.** The practice above
read class stability as a **stopping signal**; its first amendment read it as the
**repair process generating its own input**; this one names **what the input is**.
Three readings of one observation at increasing resolution — and only the third
prescribes anything, because only the third identifies something that can be
**removed**.

**★★★★★ THE SHARPENING, which is the operative half. The generator is not
"edit history in an artefact" — it is SELF-REFERENTIAL CLAIMS: claims whose truth
depends on the document's own CURRENT contents** (a set, a position, a count).
Those must be re-verified on every edit and never are. **A STATIC history claim is
safe** — *"the acceptance criterion for this Pass was `11 of 11`"* was true when
written, is true now, and no edit can falsify it. ★★ **The dangerous property is
SELF-REFERENCE, not HISTORICITY**, and that is why `R214` (a)–(d) all bite on this
file and none was sufficient: each names one **syntactic form** of self-reference,
and the supply of forms is not enumerable. **Placement is enumerable; syntax is
not.**

**⇒ THE PRACTICE, in one line: EDIT HISTORY GOES IN `ROADMAP.md` AND
`SESSION_LOG.md`, NOT IN THE ARTEFACT.** They are **append-only** (a claim there
is dated and scoped to a moment, so no later edit can falsify it), **dated** (the
reader knows what it was true of), and **read by someone looking for exactly
that** (so it has a reader who would notice). **The artefact is for the artefact.**

**★★ Corollary, earned by the round-7 note's own defect.** The replacement note
carries a wrong ordinal — *"Rounds 5 and 6 produced fresh instances of classes 1
and 2"*, under a ladder that pins round 1 to the first **correction** while every
other record in this project numbers that commit **round 3**. **It is recorded in
the `bc6c818` Shipped entry and deliberately NOT repaired**, because repairing it
writes an eighth sentence about a seventh correction. ⇒ **AN ORDINAL IS A CLAIM;
A SEQUENCE IS NOT.** Name the classes in order and the sentence asserts no count:
*"finding first wrong values, then wrong pointers, then wrong quantifiers, then an
unwritten antecedent, and finally fresh instances of the first two."* Same
content, nothing to drift. ★ **Same move as *a distance is a claim; a relation is
not*** — the repair this filing applied to its own five defective sites.

**Still practice, not a rule, and the decline is on stronger ground than before.**
`n=1` **document**; this project's bar is two occurrences. And the remedy is
**placement**, which is what this section is for — it already holds *"How a figure
is filed"* (a shape convention) and *"Librarian filing commits stay docs-only"* (a
placement convention, later promoted to `R198` at `n=2`). **`R216` stays free.**
★★★ **PROMOTION TRIGGER, written down so it can fire without anybody remembering:
a SECOND document that grows a layer of sentences about its own corrections. At
`n=2`, mint it.**

**And `R214` is NOT amended.** All four of its clauses tell you how to **write** a
self-referential claim; this tells you **not to put that class of claim in that
document**. Folding it in as clause (e) would place a **placement** rule inside a
**reference** rule and detach the remedy from the defects that motivate it — the
same argument that declined `R216` one filing ago, pointed the other way.

**Full derivation:**
`D:/dev/rag/rust/a_document_that_annotates_its_own_corrections_has_made_its_edit_history_part_of_its_content.md`
(new, 2026-08-23). **Its sibling**, amended in the same filing with round 7 and a
forward pointer:
`D:/dev/rag/rust/the_defect_class_left_after_repeated_repair_rounds_is_the_stopping_signal.md`.

#### ★★★★★ AMENDED A THIRD TIME 2026-08-23 (two-hundred-and-thirty-ninth filing, `8522167`) — THE COROLLARY'S DISPOSITION IS DISCHARGED, AND DELETION-OVER-CORRECTION GETS ITS BOUNDARY

**All three texts above are left standing** — the original practice and its two
amendments — per the append-only convention and `R215` (d).

**★★★ The corollary above is stale in one clause, and it is this role's own
defect.** It reads *"**It is recorded in the `bc6c818` Shipped entry and
deliberately NOT repaired**, because repairing it writes an eighth sentence about
a seventh correction."* **`8522167` repaired it** — by **deleting** the ordinals,
which is the remedy the same paragraph prescribes two sentences later. **The
wording is kept**; what it now means is *"not repaired **as of `bc6c818`**"*.

**★★★★★ The shape, because it is the same one this practice is about, one
indirection out: A DISPOSITION IS A CLAIM ABOUT A DOCUMENT'S CURRENT STATE, AND
IT AGES LIKE ONE.** *"Not repaired"*, *"still owed"*, *"unbuilt"*, *"carried
forward unstarted"* are self-referential in exactly the sense named above — their
truth depends on the state of something the record does not revisit. ⇒ **write a
disposition with its DATE and its subject's HASH attached** (*"not repaired as of
`bc6c818`"*), which makes it **static** and unfalsifiable by any later event.
**The same repair as the ordinals: convert a standing assertion into a dated
one.**

**★★★★★ AND THE SHARPENING THE ENGINEER ASKED FOR, ACCEPTED WITH ITS BOUNDARY:
for a SELF-REFERENTIAL claim, prefer DELETION to CORRECTION — because a
correction is drawn from the same distribution as the defect.** The only way to
say *where* or *how many* is another coordinate or another count, so a reworded
self-referential claim is a **fresh sample from the class being repaired**. This
is **not** the same statement as *"a deletion emits no new claim"*, which is true
of every deletion anywhere and supplies no mechanism.

**★★★★ THE BOUNDARY, WITHOUT WHICH IT IS A LICENCE TO DELETE CORRECTIONS
GENERALLY — and this project already holds it under another name:** *preserve
wrong VALUES, delete wrong POINTERS* (`641deb9`).

- **A self-referential claim has no value to preserve.** Its whole content is a
  coordinate into the document. Delete it and **nothing is lost** — the thing it
  pointed at is still there and can be **named**.
- **A wrong VALUE must be preserved** (`R215` (d)): a bare corrected number is
  re-derived back to the wrong one by the next reader with the same faulty
  intuition, so deleting it **destroys the evidence**.

⇒ **The rule is not *prefer deletion*. It is *prefer deletion WHEN THE CLAIM'S
CONTENT IS A COORDINATE*, and the test is whether anything is lost by removing
it.** `11 of 11` may never be deleted; *"rounds 5 and 6"* may never be corrected.

**★★ `n=2` remedies, one document** — the five *"two lines above"* distances
(`bc6c818`'s filing) and these ordinals (`8522167`), each reached the same way:
an attempt to write the corrected version produced a sentence of the same shape.
**The deletion-over-correction sharpening stays practice, not a rule; `R214` and
`R215` still not amended**, on the same placement-versus-reference ground as the
declines above.

**★★★★★ BUT THIS PRACTICE'S OWN PROMOTION TRIGGER HAS FIRED, AND THE PLACEMENT
HALF IS NOW `R216`.** The second amendment above wrote the condition down *"so it
can fire without anybody remembering"*: **a SECOND document that grows a layer of
sentences about its own corrections. At `n=2`, mint it.** The 239th filing's
own-document sweep found it: **`docs/NEXT_SESSION.md`**, carrying **three**
*"this paragraph read X until 2026-08-23"* annotations plus a running
sweep-results narrative, measured immediately before that file was rewritten.

★★★★ **And the mint says something the practice could not, because the second
instance exposed a tension between two rules rather than carelessness.** `R215`
(d) **obliges** preserving wrong wording; that is **free in an append-only file**
and means **hand-carrying it into every rewrite** of an overwritten one. ⇒
**`R216`: preserved wording and edit history belong in the append-only record; an
overwritten document carries a pointer, or nothing.** `R215` (d) is unchanged —
`R216` says **where**, not whether. **Ceiling moves `R215` → `R216`; next free
`R217`.** *(This paragraph is where the trigger's firing is recorded; the rule's
full text, its two-instance table and its scope are in **Standing rules → `R216`**.)*

**★ This practice is NOT retired by the mint.** `R216` binds **placement of a
class of content**; the practice tells you **what to look for after a repair
round** and why class stability is evidence about the repair process. They answer
different questions, and the practice's three amendments are the derivation
`R216` rests on.

**Filed into the derivation** as a sharpening of consequence 1 of
`D:/dev/rag/rust/a_document_that_annotates_its_own_corrections_has_made_its_edit_history_part_of_its_content.md`,
with the boundary beside it. **No new RAG file** — one finding per file, and this
is the same finding at higher resolution.

### Librarian filing commits stay docs-only (added 2026-08-18, hundred-and-sixty-eighth filing — FLAGGED PRACTICE, NOT A NUMBERED RULE, FIRST OCCURRENCE)

**The occurrence.** `75fa497` was the hundred-and-sixty-seventh filing's
own commit — the one that wrote the `cb20770`/`2a75be1`/`8eb0668`/
decision-070 entries `ROADMAP.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` already carry —
bundled with a `crates/pdfce-render/` correctness fix the same filing
found while reading the code (the `/BC`-vs-painted-content CMYK route
bug; see this file's `75fa497` Shipped entry). `check-commits-filed.py`
exempts a filing commit from citing its own hash **only** because a
docs-only filing cannot cite a hash that does not exist yet at commit
time. That exemption correctly does not extend to a commit that also
touches `crates/`, so this one needed a filing of its own, and CI stayed
red on exactly it until the hundred-and-sixty-eighth filing gave it one.

**The practice, stated so the regress does not recur: a librarian filing
commit should touch `docs/` only.** A finding made WHILE filing — reading
a shipped commit's own code and catching a false claim in a comment — is
real engineering work and belongs in a SEPARATE commit, made alongside
whatever else is landing that fix, not folded into the commit that writes
the filing's prose. Keeping the two apart is what makes the gate's
docs-only exemption actually exempt every filing commit, rather than
exempting most of them and creating a small, recurring category of
filings that must file themselves.

**Not promoted to a numbered rule.** No earlier instance of a filing
commit needing its own filing surfaces in this filing's read of the
record — this is the first. This project's own bar is two occurrences
before a shape earns an `R` number (see `2a75be1`'s ledger effects,
above, for the same promotion discipline applied to a different shape).
Watch for a second instance before minting one here.

> **★★★ PROMOTED 2026-08-18 (188th filing) — THIS IS NOW `R198`.** The
> trigger this entry set for itself (*"watch for a second instance"*)
> fired **four** more times: `85c9cb4` (182nd–183rd filings), `5d8eab5`
> (186th), `bea3cb1` (187th) and `3cfc5d4` (187th, final) each bundled a
> filing with `tools/` code. **Five occurrences total, four of them on
> 2026-08-18**, and the cost is measured rather than argued: **six filings
> that day tried to terminate and could not**, because each such commit is
> by construction a new unfiled code commit.
>
> ⇒ **The finding is about the record, not about commits.** This paragraph
> was correct, sat in the *Standing rules* section, was written as an
> imperative — and did not bind. ***A flagged practice is not a rule.***
> The two-occurrence bar is a bar for minting; it is not a licence to leave
> a known-correct practice unenforceable while instances pile up. **This
> entry is kept in place** (hard rule 1) as the promotion's own provenance.
> Full text and warrant table: `R198`, above.

### Pass hash vs. filing hash (added 2026-08-29, 322nd filing — CONVENTION, DELIBERATELY NOT A NUMBERED RULE)

**A `### Pass NN` entry's hash is the Pass's own CODE commit. The filing
commit that records that entry in `ROADMAP.md`/`SESSION_LOG.md` is a
DIFFERENT, LATER commit — the librarian's own commit, parented on the Pass's
code commit. The two are never expected to be equal, and their being
different is the convention working, not a discrepancy.**

Concretely, for consecutive Passes `N` and `N+1`:

```
code commit for Pass N        ──►  filing commit recording Pass N
                                        │  (child of the code commit)
                                        ▼
code commit for Pass N+1  (parent = the filing commit above)
```

So *"the commit preceding Pass `N+1`'s code commit"* and *"the hash recorded
against Pass `N`'s own entry"* name **different commits by design** — the
former is the filing commit, the latter is the code commit two steps back.
Reading them as the same figure produces a false mismatch.

**Why this is written down.** The 321st filing (`Pass 164.0`) relayed
`80b7759` as the commit preceding its own code commit (`fde9fa2`), correctly
noted it could not verify this with no shell (hard rule 8), and — rather than
stopping there — went on to flag `80b7759` as apparently contradicting
`69689c1` (`Pass 163.0`'s own recorded hash, filed one entry earlier). It
does not contradict it: `80b7759` is the *320th filing's* commit, sitting
between `69689c1` (`Pass 163.0`'s code commit) and `fde9fa2` (`Pass 164.0`'s
code commit) exactly as the diagram above predicts. The dispatcher confirmed
with `git log --oneline -6` (322nd filing) that both figures were correct
all along.

**The general lesson, kept here rather than promoted to a numbered rule
because it prescribes no check, only a naming discipline: a flagged
uncertainty is itself a claim, and it is filed into an append-only record
with the same permanence as a fact.** Flagging instead of guessing was the
right call with no shell available (hard rule 8 exists for exactly this
case) — but flagging *into the permanent record*, when the resolving command
is one line and is held by the very agent doing the dispatching, is not the
cheapest correct move available. Where a one-command verification is
reachable by asking the dispatcher before writing, ask first; reserve the
written flag for when it genuinely cannot be resolved before the filing
closes. See `SESSION_LOG.md`'s 322nd-filing entry for the correction this
produced and the full `git log` excerpt that resolved it.
